what_this_is_en: Every substance named on every line of CN106008290A, read line by line against the English rendering of each line, and asked only that: not roles, not quantities, not whether the extraction already holds it. `specific` names one substance a chemist could draw; `generic` refers to a substance without naming one, and is counted apart because "condensing agent" is sometimes an anaphor for a reagent named elsewhere and sometimes the only thing the patent ever says. Compound labels (compound I, compound II) are filed as generic on the same reasoning: the span itself names nothing, and resolving it needs a definition on another line. One entry per distinct span per line; a name repeated inside one line is not repeated here. On the "Drawn on the page" lines the drawn structures are filed under their SMILES, which is what the line literally prints. Where the English rendering carries an artefact of the vision read, the pinyin "huanhuangtong" or the literal "cyclic sulfone ketone" in place of tembotrione, the span is recorded as it appears and the canonical name is given beside it.
verified_en: Every span below was checked, by script, to be a literal substring of `source.text_en[n] or lines[n]` for its line number, which is the exact string pipeline/verify.py compares a span against. The document was therefore read in its English rendering, not in the Chinese: a Chinese span filed against a Chinese line is rejected by that check even when the reading is right. Every line from 1 to 183 is keyed, including the lines that carry no substance, whose value is an empty list. A span that is not on its line fails the build rather than reaching a reviewer. SMILES were authored only where the printed span is an abbreviation, a bare element symbol or a scanning artefact that no name parser would resolve, and only where every atom and bond is certain; everywhere else smiles is absent rather than guessed.
